title: POC Weekly: Quantization Pilot - INT8/FP8 tuning
summary: Weekly POC sync to review quantization experiment results (INT8 vs FP8), measured perf deltas and quality regressions, discuss tuning knobs and plan extended runs. Consensus: INT8 gives largest cost/latency wins with small quality drop on our eval set; FP8 shows promise for model compat but still noisy on a few prompts. Agreed next steps include longer 72-hr stability run, per-layer calibration tests, and sharing raw traces/benchmarks.
next_steps: Redwood: share benchmark spreadsheet and raw logs (Claire)
Customer: run 72-hr stability run with INT8 config and report errors (Maya)
Redwood SE: run per-layer dynamic-range calibration and send config diff (David)
Schedule deep-dive on per-prompt regressions w/ sample prompts (w/in 5 days)
action_items: Claire Morgan: upload dedicated benchmark spreadsheet + perf traces to shared drive (due 2025-02-16)
David Chu: run per-layer calibration job and attach quantization params (due 2025-02-18)
Maya Patel: start 72-hour stability run with INT8 and capture 95p latency, ERR counts (due 2025-02-19)
Raj Menon: enable extra tracing for KV cache hits/misses on pilot infra (due 2025-02-15)
transcript:
Header: 2025-02-12T16:00 PST | Duration: 42m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Claire Morgan (Redwood, AE); David Chu (Redwood, SE); Priya Shah (Redwood); Maya Patel (BrightScale, ML Lead); Raj Menon (BrightScale, SRE); Lina Gomez (BrightScale, Data Eng); Tom Erickson (BrightScale, Product)

[00:00] Claire: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on for the weekly quantization sync. quick agenda: results review, what surprised us, tuning next steps. say if i missed anything.
[00:18] Maya: no that's good, thanks. we've been running the INT8 and FP8 variants across the 5k prompt eval set you provided.
[00:30] David: cool. quick note: some of the FP8 runs initially failed on the matmul kernels — suspected underflow on a couple layers, so we applied per-layer scaling. the numbers in the summary are after that fix.
[00:46] Raj: yeah i saw some NaNs in the early logs, so thanks for the heads up.
[00:51] Claire: ok, let's walk through the headline numbers — feel free to jump in.
[00:55] David: INT8 median latency down ~35% compared to FP32 baseline on our p99-slo test harness, throughput up ~1.9x at batch size 8. tail increased slightly, p95 up ~5% in a handful of long-context prompts. FP8 showed latency improvement too but was more variable — about 20-25% median improvement, but more noise in outputs on some QA prompts.
[01:20] Maya: when you say "noise" can you give an example? we saw a handful of hallucinations on the 200-400 token answers.
[01:27] David: yeah — mostly short factual answers where confidence calibration drifted. a couple of examples where the model repeated a partial phrase or appended unrelated content. we flagged them in the sample prompts doc.
[01:38] Priya: i want to emphasize the eval harness — we're using the customer gold prompts (5k) plus a separate regression set for production-critical intents. losses reported were delta-LL and QA-F1/EM.
[01:49] Lina: F1 dropped 0.7 percentage points on INT8 vs baseline, EM ~0.4. FP8 dropped about 1.2 F1 and 0.9 EM on the same set — so INT8 is actually doing better on quality for this workload, surprise.
[02:05] Tom: cost wise what's the delta? numbers matter for procurement.
[02:09] Claire: rough op-ex: INT8 reduces GPU hours by ~48% for your workload due to higher throughput and smaller mem pressure; that maps to ~43% lower token cost on our hosted pricing model. FP8 is similar but more variable; we need longer runs to be confident.
[02:26] Raj: is that accounting for KV cache savings? our workload has high prefix reuse.
[02:31] David: yes we included KV cache hit ratios from the tracer. on INT8 the cache behavior was essentially identical; we saw slightly higher cache evictions in FP8 runs due to weight layout causing slightly larger working set in a few models we tested (probable instrumentation/packing differences).
[02:50] Maya: what's the rollout story? if we see regen or drift, can we fallback to FP32 or another variant automatically?
[02:56] Claire: yes — Redwood's routing supports automatic fallback to pinned FP32 model or to a higher-precision variant in the same model family. we can also do canary routing by percent.
[03:06] Priya: the team asked about quantization-aware prompt-specific thresholds: can we set per-intent thresholds so that for critical intents we route to FP32 immediately if delta-confidence > X?
[03:16] David: technically yes — we can add a confidence gating policy in the routing layer; it needs a small eval to calibrate thresholds, we'll propose defaults.
[03:25] Lina: about the FP8 noise: is that more from rounding or from dynamic range truncation?
[03:30] David: initial hypothesis is quantization scale placement in a few attention heads; FP8 uses a shared exponent style and if a layer has outliers, it skews scaling. per-layer calibration fixed many but not all.
[03:45] Maya: ok, on the sample prompts where we saw regressions, are those concentrated to a single domain?
[03:50] Priya: mostly finance-like factual Qs and some long-context summarization pieces — likely sensitivity to rare tokens in the tokenizer and longer KV lifetimes.
[04:02] Tom: any hits on hallucination rate by length?
[04:06] David: yes — >256 tokens had higher regression likelihood, p95 latency also increases which can compound attention truncation effects.
[04:15] Claire: let's talk stability — Raj, how did the infra behave during the overnight runs?
[04:20] Raj: cluster stable, but we saw a spike in OOMs early when we tried batch 16 with FP8 on the 70B model. after switching to contiguous weight layout and lowering batch to 12 OOMs stopped. INT8 runs never hit OOMs at batch 16 for the 70B replica.
[04:39] Maya: interesting that INT8 is both faster and more memory efficient here.
[04:43] David: INT8 benefits from smaller weight footprint and kernel paths are highly optimized in the runtime we used for these experiments; FP8 kernel still uses some fallback paths which cost mem.
[04:57] Priya: QA note — please record which code branches were used, we need commit hashes.
[05:01] Claire: yes we'll include commit + container image in the artifact.
[05:06] David: on per-prompt regressions we created a "regression bucket" doc in the shared drive with samples and model outputs; some are borderline and may be addressed by mixing-in a small FP32 ngram post-filter.
[05:23] Lina: can you explain that post-filter idea?
[05:25] David: simple run: if predicate triggers (e.g., known fact intent) then re-run generation with FP32 but with a small budget (like 50 tokens) to verify/overwrite critical spans; it's slower but it's targeted to a small subset.
[05:40] Maya: that sounds like a reasonable hybrid. what's the perf hit expected?
[05:44] Claire: depends on percent of calls falling into the predicate; if it's 5% of traffic and the FP32 check adds 0.3s avg, net p99 might grow slightly but cost could still be down vs all-FP32. we'll model this in the spreadsheet.
[05:58] Tom: for procurement we need a clear SLA for latency and quality. can we get an appendix with hit/miss rates and fallback counts?
[06:06] Claire: yes — we'll include a breakdown: p50/p95/p99, fallback counts, QoQ quality deltas at intent-level.
[06:12] Priya: a couple of small-ish noise/errors in the transcription: we saw "K V cache" spelled out in some logs — just ignore that in the notes.
[06:22] Raj: next up — tuning levers. David?
[06:25] David: first is per-layer calibration (we'll run a 1000-sample calibration to pick scale factors). second is mixed-precision: keep sensitive layers in FP16/FP32 and quantize the rest to INT8. third is batch tuning and KV cache sizing. fourth is model surgery — pruning rarely used heads (low priority).
[06:46] Maya: do you have guidance thresholds for when to prefer INT8 vs FP8?
[06:50] David: short answer: INT8 if model supports symmetric quantization and per-layer calibration — it tends to be more stable for transformer LMs. FP8 if you need to preserve some dynamic range and the runtime has robust FP8 kernels. our tests show INT8 wins here.
[07:07] Lina: on the observability side, can we get token-level deltas in the console? we want to see which tokens changed across runs.
[07:14] Priya: Redwood Console can surface token-level diffs for flagged requests; we'll add that to the demo.
[07:20] Claire: ok, let's align on the measurement plan for the 72-hour run: capture p50/p95/p99, token-level diffs for flagged intents, KV hit rates, error/NaN counts, and full traces for 1% sample. agreed?
[07:32] Maya: yes.
[07:33] Raj: agreed.
[07:34] David: agreed, i'll prepare the calibration config and the snippet to toggle the post-filter.
[07:40] Claire: any open questions from procurement or security?
[07:44] Tom: security: we need confirmation that audit logs and KMS integration are preserved in private/dedicated pilot.
[07:52] Claire: confirmed — Dedicated and Private preserve audit logs and integrate with customer KMS/HSM; we'll attach the security whitepaper.
[07:59] Tom: and data residency? for EU traffic we need region pinned.
[08:04] Claire: yes we can pin region routing and provide deployment in eu-west3 for the pilot.
[08:09] Maya: one more — can you share the raw error traces where the FP8 NaNs first appeared? we want to run an in-house repro.
[08:16] David: yes — they'll be in the traces bundle; i'll flag them in the spreadsheet.
[08:21] Priya: okay final recap?
[08:24] Claire: recap: INT8 looks like the primary candidate; FP8 useful but noisier. action items: Claire uploads artifacts; David runs per-layer calibration; Maya runs 72-hr INT8 stability test; Raj adds tracing. follow-up deep-dive on regressions scheduled next week.
[08:41] Maya: thanks everyone.
[08:43] Tom: thanks.
[08:44] Claire: bye all.

Notes: occasional mis-recognitions in automated transcript (FP8 sometimes transcribed as FFP8 or F- P 8); speaker attribution may be imperfect in a couple short interjections.
